A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete and readable, including their appendices, equations, tables, and figures. They describe the same research work, with LUViT renamed LAVIE in v3; retained and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, robustness, COCO detection and segmentation experiments, component ablations, attention analyses, and repeated-seed experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports additional DAVIS-2017, ImageNet-E, architectural ablation, and repeated-seed results.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains the ViT encoder, projected LLM block, query/value LoRA adaptation, joint MAE reconstruction objective, bidirectional attention, RoPE removal, and downstream fine-tuning. Renaming LUViT to LAVIE and testing alternative configurations do not change the default method.

E1.justification: v3 adds video object segmentation on DAVIS-2017 and ImageNet-E evaluation covering edited backgrounds, object sizes, positions, and directions. These introduce temporal prediction and additional controlled distribution shifts. ImageNet-Segmentation coverage already existed in v1's appendix and is not a new task.

E2.justification: v3 adds a fully trainable LLaMA-block comparator against frozen and LoRA-adapted alternatives in Table 6. The corresponding component-ablation table drops v1's supervised-only comparator rows, although those methods remain in Table 1. The MLP and randomly initialized LLM controls are retained; merging or renaming them does not introduce new baselines.

E3.justification: Added experiments vary LLM family and size, source-block index, block count, insertion depth, LoRA rank/alpha, and attention configuration. DAVIS evaluation introduces region-similarity and contour-accuracy metrics. These substantially expand the experimental designs, while the retained 800-epoch MAE and 100-epoch fine-tuning budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of full fine-tuning versus LoRA, alternative LLMs and layers, multiple blocks, LoRA hyperparameters, RoPE/causal attention, and insertion depth. New paired background-swap visualizations and ImageNet-E analyses further examine robustness. Conversely, the earlier component ablations' ImageNet-C results disappear.

E5.justification: v1 already includes a ten-seed ImageNet-1K analysis with reported 99% confidence intervals and a three-seed supervised-LoRA comparison. v3 removes the ten-seed analysis but broadens three-seed mean/standard-deviation reporting through Tables 1, 3, and 12–15; the supervised-LoRA standard-error table remains. Section 4's blanket seed-0 statement conflicts with several appendix captions.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the MAE baseline/proposed-method ImageNet-1K summaries from 83.2/83.6 to three-seed means of 83.11/83.63, rather than establishing a same-setting performance increase. v3 adds extensive DAVIS, ImageNet-E, and ablation results and updates segmentation summaries. COCO mask scores and ImageNet-C ablation entries disappear, while COCO box scores and ImageNet-9 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1's attention equations use WQ WK-transpose divided by sqrt(d), omitting the input features. v3 corrects them by defining Q = XWQ and K = XWK and using QK-transpose divided by sqrt(dk), in Section 5 and Appendix A.1. This is a mathematical correction; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain joint MAE/LoRA co-adaptation, improved discriminative vision performance over MAE and direct frozen-LLM fusion, and an attention-based account of background robustness. The renamed method, softened state-of-the-art wording, and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations involving overfitting under full LLM fine-tuning, optimization difficulties with two blocks, semantic maturity at deeper insertion points, and semantic priors acting as regularizers under attribute shifts. Appendix F also develops the training-versus-inference cost distinction and applicability tradeoff beyond v1's brief latency warning. These are substantial new explanations and qualifications.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement, LoRA alpha and learning-rate scheduling details, and inference FLOP/memory figures. Reported pretraining time becomes approximately 35 hours for LAVIE versus 30 for the baseline, replacing v1's approximately 30 hours for both. Exact MLP-control projection dimensions are removed, while most existing training and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: New Appendix C.4 positions LAVIE as complementary to robust ViT approaches including RVT, FAN, and MedViT. References also expand for the new datasets, LLMs, and feature-hierarchy discussion, while Picard and Lacoste references disappear with their associated sections. The central positioning relative to LM4Vision, gradient coherence, and multimodal models remains.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, consistently renames the method, numbers the method subsections, reorganizes the dense-prediction discussion, and restructures Appendix B. Existing multimodal discussion moves into Appendix C.3, while the contents pages and societal-impact section disappear. Together with substantial experimental and interpretive paragraph revisions, this exceeds a limited language edit.

P2.justification: The journal template changes typography and layout throughout. Tables are substantially restructured: classification gains reproduced-baseline rows, dense prediction combines benchmarks, and existing ablation tables are consolidated. v3 redisplays two earlier saliency examples in the main text, adds paired background-swap visualizations and new experimental tables, and removes the ten-seed uncertainty plot.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the unchanged method's empirical justification by directly testing previously untested adaptation and architectural choices, checking alternative LLMs, and extending evaluation to video and controlled attribute shifts. Broader uncertainty reporting and quantified inference costs improve assessment of reliability and practicality. These gains outweigh the loss of the ten-seed confidence-interval analysis and some earlier results/details, although conflicting seed descriptions and significance claims without a reported formal test remain weaknesses.
